Getting started with omicidxr

Sean Davis

seandavi@gmail.com

October 22, 2026

Source: vignettes/introduction.Rmd
introduction.Rmd

OmicIDX collects metadata from SRA, GEO, BioSample and BioProject and publishes it as Parquet files. omicidxr connects DuckDB to those files, so you can query tens of millions of records with SQL or dplyr without downloading them.

Installation 

if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("omicidxr")

Until omicidxr is in Bioconductor, BiocManager::install("omicidx/omicidxr") installs it from GitHub.

Connecting

omicidx_connect() returns an ordinary DuckDB DBI connection. The version argument picks the release: "latest" (the nightly build, the default), a dated nightly build "YYYY-MM-DD" (kept for 30 days), or a monthly release "YYYY-MM", which is kept long term and is the one to cite. This vignette pins the October 2026 monthly release so its results are reproducible.

library(omicidxr)

con <- omicidx_connect("2026-10")

omicidx_release() reports which release a connection is on, with the provenance from the release’s manifest.json:

release <- omicidx_release(con)
release[c("version", "publish_date", "transform_sha", "lake_snapshot_id")]
#> $version
#> [1] "2026-10"
#> 
#> $publish_date
#> [1] "2026-10-20"
#> 
#> $transform_sha
#> [1] "90688e92966330aac9ecd5a4fb8dc1d126f7982f"
#> 
#> $lake_snapshot_id
#> [1] 4171

To cite OmicIDX, cite the DOI of the monthly release you used, listed on the HuggingFace dataset page for its tag, and state the tag (2026-10).

What is in a release 

omicidx_tables(con)
#> # A tibble: 28 × 3
#>    schema    table                  type 
#>    <chr>     <chr>                  <chr>
#>  1 geometadb geo_supplemental_files VIEW 
#>  2 geometadb gpl                    VIEW 
#>  3 geometadb gse                    VIEW 
#>  4 geometadb gse_gpl                VIEW 
#>  5 geometadb gse_gsm                VIEW 
#>  6 geometadb gsm                    VIEW 
#>  7 main      bioprojects            VIEW 
#>  8 main      biosamples             VIEW 
#>  9 main      geo_platforms          VIEW 
#> 10 main      geo_samples            VIEW 
#> # ℹ 18 more rows

The sradb and geometadb schemas follow the tables of the SRAdb and GEOmetadb packages. omicidx_describe() lists a table’s columns:

omicidx_describe(con, "sradb.study")
#> # A tibble: 14 × 3
#>    column_name          column_type null 
#>    <chr>                <chr>       <chr>
#>  1 study_id             BIGINT      YES  
#>  2 study_alias          VARCHAR     YES  
#>  3 study_accession      VARCHAR     YES  
#>  4 study_title          VARCHAR     YES  
#>  5 study_type           VARCHAR     YES  
#>  6 study_abstract       VARCHAR     YES  
#>  7 broker_name          VARCHAR     YES  
#>  8 center_name          VARCHAR     YES  
#>  9 center_project_name  VARCHAR     YES  
#> 10 study_description    VARCHAR     YES  
#> 11 study_attribute      VARCHAR     YES  
#> 12 bioproject_accession VARCHAR     YES  
#> 13 geo_accession        VARCHAR     YES  
#> 14 pubmed_ids           VARCHAR[]   YES

SQL

Any DuckDB SQL works through DBI. Keep exploratory queries small with LIMIT: every query reads remote files.

DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
    SELECT study_accession, study_title
    FROM sradb.study
    WHERE study_type = 'Transcriptome Analysis'
    LIMIT 5")
#>   study_accession
#> 1       DRP000003
#> 2       DRP000004
#> 3       DRP000005
#> 4       DRP000006
#> 5       DRP000007
#>                                                                                                                                study_title
#> 1                                                Comprehensive identification and characterization of the nucleosome             structure
#> 2 Comprehensive identification and characterization of the transcripts, their             expression levels and sub-cellular localizations
#> 3 Comprehensive identification and characterization of the transcripts, their             expression levels and sub-cellular localizations
#> 4 Comprehensive identification and characterization of the transcripts, their             expression levels and sub-cellular localizations
#> 5                                      Comprehensive identification and characterization of the binding sites of             polymerase II

dplyr

omicidx_db() wraps the connection as lazy dplyr tables nested by schema, so db$sradb$<TAB> completes table names. Each table is created when first used, and nothing is read until collect().

db <- omicidx_db(con)
db
#> <omicidx_db> OmicIDX release 2026-10 (published 2026-10-20)
#> 
#> geometadb
#>   geo_supplemental_files    7,026,380
#>   gpl                          28,819
#>   gse                         293,571
#>   gse_gpl                     341,054

SRAdb and GEOmetadb helpers

A few helpers cover the common SRAdb and GEOmetadb tasks. Each runs one query and returns a tibble.

Convert accessions across SRA, GEO, BioSample and BioProject, in any direction:

sra_convert(con, "GSM4996084", c("gse", "study", "experiment", "run"))
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   study     experiment run         gse       gsm       
#>   <chr>     <chr>      <chr>       <chr>     <chr>     
#> 1 SRP299835 SRX9759115 SRR13332243 GSE164073 GSM4996084
#> 2 SRP299835 SRX9759115 SRR13332242 GSE164073 GSM4996084
#> 3 SRP299835 SRX9759115 SRR13332244 GSE164073 GSM4996084
#> 4 SRP299835 SRX9759115 SRR13332245 GSE164073 GSM4996084

List-columns

Some columns hold several values per row: in geo_search() results, type, bioprojects and sra_studies are list-columns, as are pubmed_id and contributor in geometadb.gse. tidyr::unnest_longer() gives one row per value. Rows with an empty list, such as series without SRA studies, drop out unless you pass keep_empty = TRUE:

geo_search(con, "glioblastoma", limit = 5) |>
    dplyr::select(gse, sra_studies) |>
    tidyr::unnest_longer(sra_studies)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   gse       sra_studies
#>   <chr>     <chr>      
#> 1 GSE102136 SRP114556  
#> 2 GSE108013 SRP126639

Downloading FASTQs

omicidxr finds runs; the SRA Toolkit downloads them. Write the run accessions from sra_runs() to a file:

runs <- sra_runs(con, "GSE164073")
writeLines(runs$run_accession, "runs.txt")

then fetch and convert them in a shell:

prefetch --option-file runs.txt
fasterq-dump --split-files SRR13332242

File URLs, sizes and checksums, as given by SRAdb’s listSRAfile(), are out of scope.

Migrating from SRAdb and GEOmetadb

SRAdb and GEOmetadb are deprecated. Their SQLite files had to be downloaded whole and are no longer updated. The sradb and geometadb schemas follow their tables, so most code ports by connecting with omicidx_connect() and prefixing table names with the schema.

Each SRAdb or GEOmetadb call is followed by its omicidxr equivalent:

  • getSRAdbFile(), getSQLiteFile(), then dbConnect(SQLite(), ...): con <- omicidx_connect()
  • dbGetQuery(sra_con, "SELECT * FROM study ..."): DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM sradb.study ...")
  • dbGetQuery(geo_con, "SELECT * FROM gsm ..."): DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM geometadb.gsm ...")
  • dbListTables(), dbListFields(): omicidx_tables(con), omicidx_describe(con, "sradb.run")
  • sraConvert(in_acc, out_type, sra_con): sra_convert(con, in_acc, out_type)
  • geoConvert(in_list, out_type, geo_con): geo_convert(con, in_acc, out_type)
  • getSRA(search_terms, out_types, sra_con): sra_search(con, query)
  • getSRAinfo(), listSRAfile(): sra_runs(con, in_acc), which gives run accessions for the SRA Toolkit, not file URLs (see Downloading FASTQs)
  • characteristics_ch1 parsed by hand: geo_characteristics(con, gsm)

Differences to watch for:

  • The connection comes first in every helper, so they work with |>.
  • Tables are schema-qualified: sradb.study, not study.
  • Conversion also covers BioSample and BioProject, but not SRA submissions or GEO DataSets (GDS); the marts have no submission, gds or sMatrix tables.
  • characteristics_ch1 and characteristics_ch2 are lists of tag/value pairs rather than ;\t-separated strings, and array columns such as gse.pubmed_id are lists.
  • sra_search() is a case-insensitive pattern match, not SQLite full-text search.
  • Pin a monthly release, as this vignette does, where SRAdb code pinned a SQLite file.

Disconnecting 

DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
